lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Mind the sparks, warden. Or don't — it's your face.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Blacksmith. Thirty years at this anvil, and the mine still finds ways to surprise me.

choices.text: What do you smith, with the mine sealed?

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Hoes. Hinges. Hopes. A town doesn't stop needing iron because its source stopped cooperating.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Bring ore up from a shallow level and I'll tell you what it's good for. Nothing fancy.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: I heard the hammer through three floors of rock. You finally put the big shadow down.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Foreman Hollis carried the mine on his back for twenty years. Shame what it made of him.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Knew him? I was his witness when he married. He owed me a crowbar until the end.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Now there's an old joke I can finally stop carrying. Feels worse than I thought it would.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: The miners are walking again. I've hammered ore from that vein for thirty years — never heard it scream before.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: If any of them come to my forge with that smile, send them to me. I know how to hold a heavy thing still.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: You've been swinging a pick, then. I can smell copper on a person from across the square.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Brann. Your brother would have liked the warden's answer to things. Swing first, ask after.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: The ore that comes up now sings when I quench it. Don't ask what that means. I don't know yet.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Whatever you're carrying back from the deep, don't leave it lying about my forge. Last time it walked.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: The anvil's cold for the first time in thirty years. Strange, that quiet.

lines.speaker: Gruff
lines.text: Anvil's hot. Say what you came to say.
